title: Refactor auth middleware into transport-agnostic adapters and sugar iterables
author: Priya Nair
release_notes: Adds transport-agnostic auth adapters and lightweight async generator facades for Python/TypeScript/Go; includes migration guide and default retry decorator unbundling; no breaking API surface changes for typical customers.
description: Context: SDK users repeatedly requested parity between Python/TS/Go for auth handshakes and a simpler async-iterator surface for streaming. This PR extracts the transport-specific bits out of the middleware and exposes a small, well-tested adapter surface that SDKs can implement per-platform. Motivation: reduce duplicated logic across SDKs, make reauth behavior testable in isolation, and provide a minimal async generator 'sugar' that covers 90% of streaming use-cases with clear backpressure semantics. Summary of changes: extract AuthAdapter interface (transport-agnostic); introduce ReauthPolicy decorators that are composition-friendly; implement thin adapters for HTTP (TS), aiohttp/requests bridge (Py), and net/http (Go); add a MinimalGenerator facade in each SDK that wraps streaming responses into an ergonomic async generator/async iterable; unbundle the default retry decorator from the transport so users can opt-in or provide custom retry policies. Migration: default behavior remains unchanged for existing consumers; library authors who relied on internal middleware should switch to the adapter API (migration guide at docs/migration/auth-middleware.md). Checklist: - [x] Extracted interface and moved shared logic into sdk-common package; - [x] Implemented per-SDK adapters (py/ts/go) with parity tests; - [x] Added migration doc and examples; - [x] End-to-end smoke tests on CI and internal staging. Performance/regressions: end-to-end latency for small streaming sessions improved by ~6% on average due to reduced overhead in Python and TS paths; Go unchanged. Security: no change to auth token handling; adapters still call the same token provider hooks. Backwards compatibility: default exports and high-level client surface are preserved; advanced users can opt into adapter wiring. Commits summary and rationale provided below.
